notes: meeting and therefore did not participate in the discussion or the vote.
Downtown Parking Strategy Update
Report from D. Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer

Dan Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer provided an overview of the report, including background on the development of the strategy. He indicated staff is seeking approval for partial implementation of the parking strategy as outlined in the report for 2025, subject to budget approval. He outlined the current parking enforcement strategy, the downtown shuttle service and future consideration for paid parking pilots to fund future parking supply initiatives.

D. Wilson responded to questions regarding expansion of the shuttle bus service and associated sponsorship, public engagement initiatives, and a suggested pause on the improvements to the Bissell Park parking lot.

items.title: Councillor Jefferson returned to the meeting.
notes: 2025 Preliminary Draft Capital Budget Report
Report from A. McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer
Presentation

Adam McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer introduced the 2025 preliminary draft capital budget. He outlined the topics planned to discuss at the November 5th budget meeting and indicated the 2025 draft budget book is anticipated to be made available by November 22, 2024. A. McNabb noted the Operations Centre and Bissell Park projects are not included at this time.

Mark Bradey, Manager of Finance & Deputy Treasurer provided an overview of the 2025 draft capital budget, focussing on various projects such as the Belwood Hall, Farley Neighbourhood Park, Colborne Street Reconstruction, Fourth Line Bridge 3-WG, 495 Union Street West Renovation, and the Water Meter Modernization/Replacement.

Staff responded to questions regarding the various studies including the flow of information between the advisory committees and Council, inclusion of shade features in neighbourhood parks, urbanization of Colborne Street John Street to Wilson Crescent, funding of the Fourth Line Bridge, and the future uses proposed for 495 Union Street.
Staff provided details regarding the Fergus WWTP Administration Building Expansion and the water metre modernization replacement project.
Mayor Watters called for a 10 minute recess, with the meeting resuming at 11:10 am.
A. McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services and Treasurer reviewed the various items forming the 2025 capital budget.

Staff responded to questions regarding the implementation of the municipal accommodation tax, the scope of the public engagement strategy, the development charges study, the extent of the tourism building renovations, work planned in Belsyde Cemetery, downtown Fergus streetlight replacements, the scope of the Jefferson Elora Community Centre parking lot project, signage at the Pierpoint Nature Reserve, status of the Victoria Park Elora stair replacement project, status of the Confederation Park upgrades, timing for the Churchill Crescent playground, and policies pertaining to donations or private/public partnerships.
